The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[-4,4].$ The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. It consists of three line segments. If $f(4)=12,$ calculate $f(-4).$

$f(-4)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the fundamental theorem of calculus, we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-f(-4) \\ {\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =12-f(-4) \\ f(-4) & =12-{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that the integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis.

The graph consists of $2$ parts on $[-4,4]:$ the line segments for $x\in [-4,-2]$ and two line segments for $x\in [-2,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The first integral ${A}_{1}$ represents the signed area between the line segment and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2)(2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

However, since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we take the area as negative:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{-2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-2
$$

The second integral ${A}_{2}$ represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(6)(2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of the integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =-2+6 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the value of the integral, we can find $f(-4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-4) & =12-{\int }_{-4}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =12-4 \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$
